checks: Read ce4a362fe44872e9 §4 (1) and checked its sign claims at the s=1 transition and finite cutoff.

On (0,1] pairing b with −b gives a positive derivative integral; the common endpoint b=1 has no atom. For s≥1 differentiate the explicit antiderivative at fixed s using ∂a q=s. Combining terms gives the displayed numerator F(q)−(1−da)(1−a)^{−d}.

F(q) is positive, strictly decreasing for q>1 and tends to zero. The numerator starts positive at q=1+a; if a<1/d it ends negative, giving one root. The boundary a=1/d stays positive at every finite slope.

The proper cutoff U has T=U/r(U). When T≥1 the frustum moment equals the cone moment through T and is T/s times its value at T above T. The condition T<s* is strict, so it excludes a root at the cutoff and a zero tail there.
At s=0 the coarea is positive and the correction is defined. Both that record and the optional infinity record have corrected mass V/2.
